newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn falls to fresh two-year lows.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn falls to fresh two-year lows.

text.p: CBOT corn futures fell to new contract lows and fresh two-year lows by midsession on near-perfect crop weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
Recent warm temperatures and showers have boosted crop production prospects and there have been no outlooks to indicate a shift away from the good crop growing conditions.
The new low for July is $2.48 per bushel, below the previous low of $2.50 set Thursday and the lowest level for a nearby contract since May 1995.
Also a new low was set in new crop December.
The new low for December is $2.36-1/4, below the previous low of $2.38-1/4 set Thursday.
Position squaring was noted before numerous key reports are released, traders said.
USDA releases its updated hogs and pigs report today and the updated USDA stocks and acreage reports on Monday. Monday is also first notice day for deliveries on the July contract.
At 1104 CDT, corn was one to two cents per bushel lower, with July down 1-3/4 at $2.48-1/2.
Lind Waldock sold three million bushels of December, traders said. Cargill Inc, Continental Grain and Refco Inc each sold one million bushels of December, traders said.
Continental Grain bear spread two million bushels of December/July at 11-3/4 cents, premium July, traders said. Cargill Inc bought 2.5 million bushels of July, traders said.
